rows.description: A friend sees someone gasping, shaking and saying they cannot breathe, and worries something terrible is happening. Staying near, speaking slowly and keeping the surroundings calm helps, and medical help is right if it seems serious.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anxiety, calm, relief from stress

rows.subtype: Panic in a crowded or stressful place [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult in a packed train or exam hall feels heat, tingling, tight chest and a need to escape. Slow breathing, feeling something solid and remembering the wave will crest help until it passes.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: relief from stress

rows.description: A helper stays calm, uses simple short sentences, does not say just relax, and lets the person choose to sit or move outside. Afterwards they encourage a check-up to rule out physical causes and to find support.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: calm

rows.description: A working adult who has had repeated panic episodes may plan life around avoiding triggers, feeling ashamed and secretive. Recovery is common with proper professional guidance, and telling one trusted person eases the load.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: shame, trust

rows.description: A toddler's fury shows up as stiff body, red face, hitting or throwing because the brain has no brakes yet. Staying calm, keeping the child safe and waiting teaches more than punishment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, calm, trust

rows.subtype: Child learning what anger feels like [Actor]
rows.description: A young child feels hot cheeks, clenched fists and a fast heart before an outburst. Helping the child notice these signs, with words like I see your fists are tight, lays the base for later self-control.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger

rows.description: A parent facing a shouting child may respond louder, which escalates the storm. Lowering the voice, pausing and returning to the conversation once both are calm models the skill being asked of the child.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, calm

rows.description: A teenager provoked by a sibling or teacher feels heat, pounding pulse and tunnel vision, and may say things that cannot be unsaid. Walking away, cold water or a run allows the surge to fall before speaking.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger

rows.subtype: Hostel argument that got out of hand [Receiver]
rows.description: A young adult on the receiving end of shouted words feels shock, fear or a rising wish to hit back. Keeping distance and refusing to match the volume protects safety and often lets the other person deflate.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear, surprise, trust

rows.description: A mature person notices anger in the body, says I need a break, and returns later to talk about the problem without blaming. Cooling down is not avoidance if the issue is honestly revisited.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: anger
related concepts: avoidance
